(125)

The density operator ℛB→B​C​(ρA^​A​Bp)\mathcal{R}_{B\to BC}(\rho^{p}_{\hat{A}AB}) can be written as

ℛB→B​C​(ρA^​A​Bp)=(1−p)​|0⟩​⟨0|A^⊗ℛB→B​C​(ρA​B0)+p|1⟩​⟨1|A^⊗ℛB→B​C​(ρA​B).\displaystyle\mathcal{R}_{B\to BC}(\rho^{p}_{\hat{A}AB})=(1-p)|0\rangle\!\langle 0|_{\hat{A}}\otimes\mathcal{R}_{B\to BC}(\rho^{0}_{AB})+p|1\rangle\!\langle 1|_{\hat{A}}\otimes\mathcal{R}_{B\to BC}(\rho_{AB})\ . (126)

The relevant density operators thus satisfy the orthogonality conditions for equality in Lemma A.1, from which (125) follows. Furthermore, as explained in the proof of Lemma 3.2 we have

I(A^A:C|B)ρp=(1−p)I(A:C|B)ρ0+pI(A:C|B)ρ.\displaystyle I(\hat{A}A:C|B)_{\rho^{p}}=(1-p)I(A:C|B)_{\rho^{0}}+pI(A:C|B)_{\rho}\ . (127)

Equations (125) and (127) imply that

Δ~ℛ​(ρp)=(1−p)​Δ~ℛ​(ρ0)+p​Δ~ℛ​(ρ).\displaystyle\tilde{\Delta}_{\mathcal{R}}(\rho^{p})=(1-p)\tilde{\Delta}_{\mathcal{R}}(\rho^{0})+p\tilde{\Delta}_{\mathcal{R}}(\rho)\ . (128)

We next verify that Δ~ℛ​(⋅)\tilde{\Delta}_{\mathcal{R}}(\cdot) fulfills Property 2. Let ℛB→B​C,ℛB→B​C′∈TPCP⁡(B,B⊗C)\mathcal{R}_{B\to BC},\mathcal{R}^{\prime}_{B\to BC}\in\mathrm{TPCP}(B,B\otimes C), α∈[0,1]\alpha\in[0,1] and ℛ¯B→B​C=α​ℛB→B​C+(1−α)​ℛB→B​C′\bar{\mathcal{R}}_{B\to BC}=\alpha\mathcal{R}_{B\to BC}+(1-\alpha)\mathcal{R}^{\prime}_{B\to BC}. Lemma A.1 implies that for any state ρA​B​C\rho_{ABC} on A⊗B⊗CA\otimes B\otimes C

F(ρA​B​C,ℛ¯B→B​C(ρA​B))=F(ρA​B​C,αℛB→B​C(ρA​B)+(1−α)ℛ′B→B​C(ρA​B))≥α​F​(ρA​B​C,ℛB→B​C​(ρA​B))+(1−α)​F​(ρA​B​C,ℛB→B​C′​(ρA​B)),F\bigl(\rho_{ABC},\bar{\mathcal{R}}_{B\to BC}(\rho_{AB})\bigr)=F\bigl(\rho_{ABC},\alpha\mathcal{R}_{B\to BC}(\rho_{AB})+(1-\alpha)\mathcal{R}^{\prime}_{B\to BC}(\rho_{AB})\bigl)\\ \geq\alpha F\bigl(\rho_{ABC},\mathcal{R}_{B\to BC}(\rho_{AB})\bigr)+(1-\alpha)F\bigl(\rho_{ABC},\mathcal{R}^{\prime}_{B\to BC}(\rho_{AB})\bigr)\ , (129)

and, hence by the definition of Δ~ℛ​(⋅)\tilde{\Delta}_{\mathcal{R}}(\cdot)

Δ~ℛ¯​(ρ)≥α​Δ~ℛ​(ρ)+(1−α)​Δ~ℛ′​(ρ).\displaystyle\tilde{\Delta}_{\bar{\mathcal{R}}}(\rho)\geq\alpha\tilde{\Delta}_{\mathcal{R}}(\rho)+(1-\alpha)\tilde{\Delta}_{\mathcal{R}^{\prime}}(\rho)\ . (130)

The function ρ↦Δ~ℛ​(ρ)\rho\mapsto\tilde{\Delta}_{\mathcal{R}}(\rho) is continuous which clearly implies Property 3. To see this, recall that by the Alicki-Fannes inequality ρ↦I(A:C|B)ρ\rho\mapsto I(A:C|B)_{\rho} is continuous for a finite-dimensional CC system [1]. Furthermore, since ρA​B↦ℛB​C​(ρA​B)\rho_{AB}\mapsto\mathcal{R}_{BC}(\rho_{AB}) is continuous (see Lemma C.5), Lemma B.9 of [11] implies that ρA​B​C↦F⁡(ρA​B​C,ℛB→B​C​(ρA​B))\rho_{ABC}\mapsto F(\rho_{ABC},\mathcal{R}_{B\to BC}(\rho_{AB})) is continuous, which then establishes Property 3.

Finally it remains to show that Δ~ℛ​(⋅)\tilde{\Delta}_{\mathcal{R}}(\cdot) satisfies Property 4, which however follows directly by Lemma C.4.

∎

Let 𝒫⊆TPCP⁡(B,B⊗C)\mathcal{P}\subseteq\mathrm{TPCP}(B,B\otimes C) be the convex hull of the set of trace-preserving completely positive mappings from the BB to the B⊗CB\otimes C system that are of the form (112). We note that the elements of 𝒫\mathcal{P} are mappings of the form (10), since a convex combination of unitary mappings are unital and a convex combination of trace-preserving maps remains trace-preserving. Proposition 3.1, which is applicable as shown in Lemma 5.2 together with Step 1 therefore proves the assertion for a fixed AA system.

Step 3: Independence from the AA system

Let 𝒮\mathcal{S} be the set of all density operators on A¯⊗B⊗C\bar{A}\otimes B\otimes C with a fixed marginal ρB​C\rho_{BC} on B⊗CB\otimes C, where BB and CC are finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces and A¯\bar{A} is the infinite-dimensional Hilbert space ℓ2\ell^{2} of square summable sequences.

We note that the set of trace-preserving completely positive maps of the form (10) on finite-dimensional systems is compact, which follows by Remark C.3 together with the fact that the intersection of a compact set and a closed set is compact. Hence, using Lemma 5.2 (in particular Properties 3 and 4) and the result from Step 2 above, the same argument as in Step 4 of Section 3 can be applied to conclude the existence of a recovery map ℛB→B​C\mathcal{R}_{B\to BC} of the form (10) such that Δ~ℛ​(𝒮)≥0\tilde{\Delta}_{\mathcal{R}}(\mathcal{S})\geq 0.

As every separable Hilbert space AA can isometrically embedded into A¯\bar{A} [26, Theorem II.7] and since Δ~ℛ¯\tilde{\Delta}_{\bar{\mathcal{R}}} is invariant under isometries applied on the extension space AA, we can conclude that the recovery map ℛB→B​C\mathcal{R}_{B\to BC} remains valid for any separable extension space AA. This proves the statement of Corollary 2.4 for finite-dimensional BB and CC systems.

6 Discussion

Our main result is that for any density operator ρB​C\rho_{BC} on B⊗CB\otimes C there exists a recovery map ℛB→B​C\mathcal{R}_{B\to BC} such that the distance between any extension ρA​B​C\rho_{ABC} of ρB​C\rho_{BC} acting on A⊗B⊗CA\otimes B\otimes C and ℛB→B​C​(ρA​B)\mathcal{R}_{B\to BC}(\rho_{AB}) is bounded from above by the conditional mutual information I(A:C|B)ρI(A:C|B)_{\rho}. It is natural to ask whether such a map can be described as a simple and explicit function of ρB​C\rho_{BC}. In fact, it was conjectured in [20, 4] that (2) holds for a very simple choice of map, namely

𝒯B→B​C:XB↦ρB​C12​(ρB−12​XB​ρB−12⊗idC)​ρB​C12,\displaystyle\mathcal{T}_{B\to BC}\,:\,X_{B}\mapsto\rho_{BC}^{\frac{1}{2}}(\rho_{B}^{-\frac{1}{2}}X_{B}\rho_{B}^{-\frac{1}{2}}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{C})\rho_{BC}^{\frac{1}{2}}\ , (131)

called the transpose map or Petz recovery map. This conjecture, if correct, would have important consequences in obtaining remainder terms for the monotonicity of the relative entropy [3]. As discussed in the introduction, if ρA​B​C\rho_{ABC} is such that it is a (perfect) quantum Markov chain or the BB system is classical, the claim of the conjecture is known to hold.

One possible approach to prove a result of this form would be to start from the result (2) for an unknown recovery map and then show that the transpose map 𝒯B→B​C\mathcal{T}_{B\to BC} cannot be much worse than any other recovery map. In fact, a theorem of Barnum and Knill [2] directly implies that when ρA​B​C\rho_{ABC} is pure, we have

F⁡(ρA​B​C,𝒯B→B​C​(ρA​B))≤F​(A;C|B)ρ≤F⁡(ρA​B​C,𝒯B→B​C​(ρA​B)).\displaystyle F\big(\rho_{ABC},\mathcal{T}_{B\to BC}(\rho_{AB})\big)\leq F(A;C|B)_{\rho}\leq\sqrt{F\big(\rho_{ABC},\mathcal{T}_{B\to BC}(\rho_{AB})\big)}\ . (132)

This shows that, if ρA​B​C\rho_{ABC} is pure, an inequality of the form (2), with the fidelity replaced by its square root, holds for the transpose map. In order to generalize this to all states, one might hope that (132) also holds for mixed states ρA​B​C\rho_{ABC}. However, this turns out to be wrong even when the state ρA​B​C\rho_{ABC} is completely classical (see Appendix F for an example).

Another interesting question is whether the lower bound in terms of the measured relative entropy (8) can be improved to a relative entropy. Such an inequality is known to be false if we restrict the recovery map to be the transpose map (131) [35], but it might be true when we optimize over all recovery maps. It is worth noting that in case such an inequality holds for any ρA​B​C\rho_{ABC} and a corresponding recovery map, then the argument presented in this work would imply that there exists a universal recovery map satisfying (8) with the relative entropy instead of the measured relative entropy. This can be seen by defining the function family ρ↦Δℛ(ρ):=I(A:C|B)ρ−D(ρA​B​C||ℛB→B​C(ρA​B))\rho\mapsto\Delta_{\mathcal{R}}(\rho):=I(A:C|B)_{\rho}-D(\rho_{ABC}|\hskip-1.13809pt|\mathcal{R}_{B\to BC}(\rho_{AB})). Lemma B.2, the convexity of the relative entropy [23, Theorem 11.12] and the lower semicontinuity of the relative entropy [18, Example 7.22] imply that Δℛ​(⋅)\Delta_{\mathcal{R}}(\cdot) satisfies Properties 1-4. As a result, Proposition 3.1 is applicable which can be used to prove the existence of a universal recovery map.

Appendices

Appendix A General facts about the fidelity

The following lemma states a standard concavity property of the fidelity which is presented here for completeness and since we are interested in the case where equality holds.

Lemma A.1.

For any density operators ρ\rho, ρ′\rho^{\prime}, σ\sigma, and σ′\sigma^{\prime}, and for any p∈[0,1]p\in[0,1] we have

F⁡(p​ρ+(1−p)​ρ′,p​σ+(1−p)​σ′)≥p​F​(ρ,σ)+(1−p)​F​(ρ′,σ′),\displaystyle F\bigl(p\rho+(1-p)\rho^{\prime},p\sigma+(1-p)\sigma^{\prime}\bigr)\geq pF(\rho,\sigma)+(1-p)F(\rho^{\prime},\sigma^{\prime})\ , (133)

with equality if both of ρ\rho and σ\sigma are orthogonal to both of ρ′\rho^{\prime} and σ′\sigma^{\prime}.

Proof.

Note first that for any two normalized and mutually orthogonal vectors |0⟩|0\rangle and |1⟩|1\rangle in an ancilla space, we have

F⁡(p​ρ+(−p)​ρ′,p​σ+(1−p)​σ′)≥F⁡(p​ρ⊗|0⟩​⟨0|+(−p)​ρ′⊗|1⟩​⟨1|,p​σ⊗|0⟩​⟨0|+(1−p)​σ′⊗|1⟩​⟨1|),\displaystyle F\bigl(p\rho\!+\!(1\!-\!p)\rho^{\prime},p\sigma\!+\!(1-p)\sigma^{\prime}\bigr)\geq F\bigl(p\rho\!\otimes\!|0\rangle\!\langle 0|\!+\!(1\!-\!p)\rho^{\prime}\!\otimes\!|1\rangle\!\langle 1|,p\sigma\!\otimes\!|0\rangle\!\langle 0|+(1-p)\sigma^{\prime}\!\otimes\!|1\rangle\!\langle 1|\bigr)\ , (134)

because of the monotonicity of the fidelity under the partial trace. Furthermore, if both of ρ\rho and σ\sigma are orthogonal to both of ρ′\rho^{\prime} and σ′\sigma^{\prime} then there exists a trace-preserving completely positive map that generates the corresponding state |0⟩|0\rangle or |1⟩|1\rangle of the ancilla system. This implies that, in this case, the inequality also holds in the other direction. It therefore suffices to prove (133) with ρ\rho and σ\sigma replaced by ρ⊗|0⟩​⟨0|\rho\otimes|0\rangle\!\langle 0| and σ⊗|0⟩​⟨0|\sigma\otimes|0\rangle\!\langle 0|, and with ρ′\rho^{\prime} and σ′\sigma^{\prime} replaced by ρ′⊗|1⟩​⟨1|\rho^{\prime}\otimes|1\rangle\!\langle 1| and σ′⊗|1⟩​⟨1|\sigma^{\prime}\otimes|1\rangle\!\langle 1|, respectively. In other words, it remains to show that, for the case where ρ\rho and σ\sigma are orthogonal to ρ′\rho^{\prime} and σ′\sigma^{\prime}, (133) holds with equality, i.e.,

F⁡(ρ¯,σ¯)=p​F​(ρ,σ)+(1−p)​F​(ρ′,σ′),\displaystyle F(\bar{\rho},\bar{\sigma})=pF(\rho,\sigma)+(1-p)F(\rho^{\prime},\sigma^{\prime})\ , (135)

where ρ¯=p​ρ+(1−p)​ρ′\bar{\rho}=p\rho+(1-p)\rho^{\prime} and σ¯=p​σ+(1−p)​σ′\bar{\sigma}=p\sigma+(1-p)\sigma^{\prime}.

For this, let |ϕ⟩|\phi\rangle, |ϕ′⟩|\phi^{\prime}\rangle, |ψ⟩|\psi\rangle, and |ψ′⟩|\psi^{\prime}\rangle be purifications of ρ\rho, ρ′\rho^{\prime}, σ\sigma, and σ′\sigma^{\prime}, respectively, such that F⁡(ρ,σ)=⟨ϕ|ψ⟩F(\rho,\sigma)=\langle\phi|\psi\rangle and F⁡(ρ′,σ′)=⟨ϕ′|ψ′⟩F(\rho^{\prime},\sigma^{\prime})=\langle\phi^{\prime}|\psi^{\prime}\rangle. It is easy to verify that

|ϕ¯⟩=p​|ϕ⟩⊗|0⟩+1−p​|ϕ′⟩⊗|1⟩and|ψ¯⟩=p​|ψ⟩⊗|0⟩+1−p​|ψ′⟩⊗|1⟩\displaystyle|\bar{\phi}\rangle=\sqrt{p}|\phi\rangle\otimes|0\rangle+\sqrt{1-p}|\phi^{\prime}\rangle\otimes|1\rangle\quad\text{and}\quad|\bar{\psi}\rangle=\sqrt{p}|\psi\rangle\otimes|0\rangle+\sqrt{1-p}|\psi^{\prime}\rangle\otimes|1\rangle (136)

are purifications of ρ¯\bar{\rho} and of σ¯\bar{\sigma}, respectively. Hence,

p​F​(ρ,σ)+(1−p)​F​(ρ′,σ′)=p⁡⟨ϕ|ψ⟩+(1−p)​⟨ϕ′​|ψ′⟩=⟨ϕ¯|​ψ¯⟩≤F⁡(ρ¯,σ¯),\displaystyle pF(\rho,\sigma)+(1-p)F(\rho^{\prime},\sigma^{\prime})=p\langle\phi|\psi\rangle+(1-p)\langle\phi^{\prime}|\psi^{\prime}\rangle=\langle\bar{\phi}|\bar{\psi}\rangle\leq F(\bar{\rho},\bar{\sigma})\ , (137)

which proves one direction of (135).

To prove the other direction, let π\pi be the projector onto the joint support of ρ\rho and σ\sigma, i.e., π​ρ=ρ\pi\rho=\rho and π​σ=σ\pi\sigma=\sigma. Similarly, let π′\pi^{\prime} be the projector onto the joint support of ρ′\rho^{\prime} and σ′\sigma^{\prime}, i.e,. π′​ρ′=ρ′\pi^{\prime}\rho^{\prime}=\rho^{\prime} and π′​σ′=σ′\pi^{\prime}\sigma^{\prime}=\sigma^{\prime}. By the condition that ρ\rho and σ\sigma are orthogonal to ρ′\rho^{\prime} and σ′\sigma^{\prime}, the two projectors must be orthogonal, i.e., π​π′=0\pi\pi^{\prime}=0. Furthermore, let |ϕ¯⟩|\bar{\phi}\rangle be a purification of ρ¯\bar{\rho} and let |ψ¯⟩|\bar{\psi}\rangle be a purification of σ¯\bar{\sigma} such that F⁡(ρ¯,σ¯)=⟨ϕ¯|ψ¯⟩F(\bar{\rho},\bar{\sigma})=\langle\bar{\phi}|\bar{\psi}\rangle. Because

p​ρ=π​ρ¯​πand(1−p)​ρ′=π′​ρ¯​π′\displaystyle p\rho=\pi\bar{\rho}\pi\quad\text{and}\quad(1-p)\rho^{\prime}=\pi^{\prime}\bar{\rho}\pi^{\prime} (138)

π​|ϕ¯⟩\pi|\bar{\phi}\rangle and π′​|ϕ¯⟩\pi^{\prime}|\bar{\phi}\rangle are purifications of p​ρp\rho and (1−p)​ρ′(1-p)\rho^{\prime}, respectively. Similarly, π​|ψ¯⟩\pi|\bar{\psi}\rangle and π′​|ψ¯⟩\pi^{\prime}|\bar{\psi}\rangle are purifications of p​σp\sigma and (1−p)​σ′(1-p)\sigma^{\prime}, respectively. Hence, we have

F⁡(ρ¯,σ¯)=⟨ϕ¯|ψ¯⟩=⟨ϕ¯|π⁡|ψ¯⟩+⟨ϕ¯|​π′|ψ¯⟩≤F⁡(p​ρ,p​σ)+F⁡((1−p)​ρ′,(1−p)​σ′)=p​F​(ρ,σ)+(1−p)​F​(ρ′,σ′).F(\bar{\rho},\bar{\sigma})=\langle\bar{\phi}|\bar{\psi}\rangle=\langle\bar{\phi}|\pi|\bar{\psi}\rangle+\langle\bar{\phi}|\pi^{\prime}|\bar{\psi}\rangle\leq F\bigl(p\rho,p\sigma\bigr)+F\bigl((1-p)\rho^{\prime},(1-p)\sigma^{\prime}\bigr)\\ =pF(\rho,\sigma)+(1-p)F(\rho^{\prime},\sigma^{\prime})\ . (139)

This proves the other direction of (135) and thus concludes the proof. ∎

The following lemma generalizes the Fuchs-van de Graaf inequality which has been proven for states to non-negative operators. The result is standard and stated here for completeness.

Lemma A.2.

For any two non-negative operators ρ\rho and σ\sigma with tr⁡(ρ)≥tr⁡(σ)\mathrm{tr}(\rho)\geq\mathrm{tr}(\sigma), the trace norm of their difference is bounded from above by

‖ρ−σ‖1≤2​tr​(ρ)2−F​(ρ,σ)2.\displaystyle\left\lVert\rho-\sigma\right\rVert_{1}\leq 2\sqrt{\mathrm{tr}(\rho)^{2}-F(\rho,\sigma)^{2}}\ . (140)
Proof.

Let ω\omega be a non-negative operator with tr⁡(ω)=tr⁡(ρ)−tr⁡(σ)\mathrm{tr}(\omega)=\mathrm{tr}(\rho)-\mathrm{tr}(\sigma), whose support is orthogonal to the support of both ρ\rho and σ\sigma, and define σ′=σ+ω\sigma^{\prime}=\sigma+\omega. Then tr⁡(ρ)=tr⁡(σ′)\mathrm{tr}(\rho)=\mathrm{tr}(\sigma^{\prime}) and

‖ρ−σ‖1=‖ρ−σ′‖1andF⁡(ρ,σ)=F⁡(ρ,σ′).\displaystyle\left\lVert\rho-\sigma\right\rVert_{1}=\left\lVert\rho-\sigma^{\prime}\right\rVert_{1}\qquad\text{and}\qquad F(\rho,\sigma)=F(\rho,\sigma^{\prime})\ . (141)

It therefore suffices to show that the claim holds for operators with tr⁡(ρ)=tr⁡(σ)=c∈ℝ+\mathrm{tr}(\rho)=\mathrm{tr}(\sigma)=c\in\mathbb{R}^{+}. Furthermore for c>0c>0, defining ρ¯=ρ/c\bar{\rho}=\rho/c and σ¯=σ/c\bar{\sigma}=\sigma/c and noting that

‖ρ−σ‖1=c​‖ρ¯−σ¯‖1andF⁡(ρ,σ)=c​F​(ρ¯,σ¯),\displaystyle\left\lVert\rho-\sigma\right\rVert_{1}=c\left\lVert\bar{\rho}-\bar{\sigma}\right\rVert_{1}\qquad\text{and}\qquad F(\rho,\sigma)=cF(\bar{\rho},\bar{\sigma})\ , (142)

it suffices to verify that the claim holds for tr⁡(ρ)=tr⁡(σ)=1\mathrm{tr}(\rho)=\mathrm{tr}(\sigma)=1 which follows by the Fuchs-van de Graaf inequality [12]. ∎

Appendix B General facts about the measured relative entropy

Definition B.1.

The measured relative entropy between density operators ρ\rho and σ\sigma is defined as the supremum of the relative entropy with measured inputs over all POVMs ℳ={Mx}\mathcal{M}=\{M_{x}\}, i.e.,

D𝕄(ρ||σ)=sup{D(ℳ(ρ)||ℳ(σ)):ℳ(ρ)=∑xtr(ρMx)|x⟩⟨x| with ∑xMx=id},\displaystyle D_{\mathbb{M}}(\rho|\hskip-1.13809pt|\sigma)=\sup\bigl\{D(\mathcal{M}(\rho)|\hskip-1.13809pt|\mathcal{M}(\sigma)):\mathcal{M}(\rho)=\sum_{x}\mathrm{tr}(\rho M_{x})|x\rangle\!\langle x|\text{ with }\sum_{x}M_{x}=\mathrm{id}\bigr\}\ , (143)

where {|x⟩}\{|x\rangle\} is a finite set of orthonormal vectors.

This quantity was studied in [17, 15] where it was shown that 1nD𝕄(ρ⊗n||σ⊗n)\frac{1}{n}D_{\mathbb{M}}(\rho^{\otimes n}|\hskip-1.13809pt|\sigma^{\otimes n}) converges to the relative entropy D(ρ||σ):=tr(ρ(logρ−logσ))D(\rho|\hskip-1.13809pt|\sigma):=\mathrm{tr}(\rho(\log\rho-\log\sigma)).

Lemma B.2.

Let ρ\rho, ρ′\rho^{\prime}, σ\sigma, and σ′\sigma^{\prime} be density operators such that both ρ\rho and σ\sigma are orthogonal to both ρ′\rho^{\prime} and σ′\sigma^{\prime}. For any p∈[0,1]p\in[0,1] we have

D(pρ+(1−p)ρ′||pσ+(1−p)σ′)=pD(ρ||σ)+(1−p)D(ρ′||σ′).\displaystyle D\bigl(p\rho+(1-p)\rho^{\prime}\,|\hskip-1.13809pt|\,p\sigma+(1-p)\sigma^{\prime}\bigr)=pD(\rho|\hskip-1.13809pt|\sigma)+(1-p)D(\rho^{\prime}|\hskip-1.13809pt|\sigma^{\prime})\ . (144)
Proof.

By the orthogonality of ρ\rho and ρ′\rho^{\prime} (respectively σ\sigma and σ′\sigma^{\prime}) we have

log⁡(p​ρ+(1−p)​ρ′)=log⁡(p​ρ)+log⁡((1−p)​ρ′)=log⁡(p)+log⁡(1−p)+log⁡(ρ)+log⁡(ρ′)\displaystyle\log\bigl(p\rho+(1-p)\rho^{\prime}\bigr)=\log(p\rho)+\log\bigl((1-p)\rho^{\prime}\bigr)=\log(p)+\log(1-p)+\log(\rho)+\log(\rho^{\prime}) (145)

and ρ​log⁡ρ′=0\rho\log\rho^{\prime}=0. Thus by definition of the relative entropy we obtain the desired statement. ∎

Lemma B.3.

Let ρ\rho, ρ′\rho^{\prime}, σ\sigma, and σ′\sigma^{\prime} be density operators such that both ρ\rho and σ\sigma are orthogonal to both ρ′\rho^{\prime} and σ′\sigma^{\prime}. For any p∈[0,1]p\in[0,1] we have

D𝕄(pρ+(1−p)ρ′||pσ+(1−p)σ′)=pD𝕄(ρ||σ)+(1−p)D𝕄(ρ′||σ′).\displaystyle D_{\mathbb{M}}\bigl(p\rho+(1-p)\rho^{\prime}\,|\hskip-1.13809pt|\,p\sigma+(1-p)\sigma^{\prime}\bigr)=pD_{\mathbb{M}}(\rho|\hskip-1.13809pt|\sigma)+(1-p)D_{\mathbb{M}}(\rho^{\prime}|\hskip-1.13809pt|\sigma^{\prime})\ . (146)
Proof.

Let ℳ={Mx}\mathcal{M}=\{M_{x}\}, ℳ′={My′}\mathcal{M}^{\prime}=\{M^{\prime}_{y}\} be measurements and define the POVM on 𝒩\mathcal{N} whose elements are given by {Mx}x∪{My′}y\{M_{x}\}_{x}\cup\{M^{\prime}_{y}\}_{y}. Then we can write

𝒩⁡(p​ρ+(1−p)​ρ′)\displaystyle\mathcal{N}\bigl(p\rho+(1-p)\rho^{\prime}\bigr) =p​∑xtr⁡(Mx​ρ)​|x⟩​⟨x|+(1−p)​∑ytr⁡(My′​ρ′)​|y⟩​⟨y|.\displaystyle=p\sum_{x}\mathrm{tr}(M_{x}\rho)|x\rangle\!\langle x|+(1-p)\sum_{y}\mathrm{tr}(M^{\prime}_{y}\rho^{\prime})|y\rangle\!\langle y|\ . (147)

As a result using Lemma B.2,

D𝕄(pρ+(1−p)ρ′||pσ+(1−p)σ′)≥D(𝒩(pρ+(1−p)ρ′)||𝒩(pσ+(1−p)σ′))=p​D​(∑xtr⁡(Mx​ρ)​|x⟩​⟨x|​||∑xtr⁡(Mx​σ)|​x⟩​⟨x|)+(1−p)​D​(∑ytr⁡(My′​ρ′)​|y⟩​⟨y|​||∑ytr⁡(My′​σ′)|​y⟩​⟨y|).D_{\mathbb{M}}\bigl(p\rho+(1-p)\rho^{\prime}\,|\hskip-1.13809pt|\,p\sigma+(1-p)\sigma^{\prime}\bigr)\geq D\Bigl(\mathcal{N}\bigl(p\rho+(1-p)\rho^{\prime}\bigr)\,\Big|\hskip-1.70717pt\Big|\,\mathcal{N}\bigl(p\sigma+(1-p)\sigma^{\prime}\bigr)\Bigr)\\ =pD\Bigl(\sum_{x}\mathrm{tr}(M_{x}\rho)|x\rangle\!\langle x|\Big|\hskip-1.70717pt\Big|\sum_{x}\mathrm{tr}(M_{x}\sigma)|x\rangle\!\langle x|\Bigr)+(1-p)D\Bigl(\sum_{y}\mathrm{tr}(M^{\prime}_{y}\rho^{\prime})|y\rangle\!\langle y|\Big|\hskip-1.70717pt\Big|\sum_{y}\mathrm{tr}(M^{\prime}_{y}\sigma^{\prime})|y\rangle\!\langle y|\Bigr)\ . (148)

As this inequality is valid for any measurements ℳ\mathcal{M} and ℳ′\mathcal{M}^{\prime}, taking the supremum over such measurements gives

D𝕄(pρ+(1−p)ρ′||pσ+(1−p)σ′)≥pD𝕄(ρ||σ)+(1−p)D𝕄(ρ′||σ′).\displaystyle D_{\mathbb{M}}\bigl(p\rho+(1-p)\rho^{\prime}\,|\hskip-1.13809pt|\,p\sigma+(1-p)\sigma^{\prime}\bigr)\geq pD_{\mathbb{M}}(\rho|\hskip-1.13809pt|\sigma)+(1-p)D_{\mathbb{M}}(\rho^{\prime}|\hskip-1.13809pt|\sigma^{\prime})\ . (149)

For the other direction, consider a measurement ℳ={Mx}\mathcal{M}=\{M_{x}\}. We can write

ℳ⁡(p​ρ+(1−p)​ρ′)\displaystyle\mathcal{M}\bigl(p\rho+(1-p)\rho^{\prime}\bigr) =∑xp​tr​(Mx​ρ)​|x⟩​⟨x|+(1−p)​tr​(Mx​ρ′)|x⟩​⟨x|.\displaystyle=\sum_{x}p\,\mathrm{tr}(M_{x}\rho)|x\rangle\!\langle x|+(1-p)\,\mathrm{tr}(M_{x}\rho^{\prime})|x\rangle\!\langle x|\ . (150)

Combining this with the joint convexity of the relative entropy [23, Theorem 11.12], we get

D𝕄(pρ+(1−p)ρ′||pσ+(1−p)σ′)=D(ℳ(pρ+(1−p)ρ′)||ℳ(pσ+(1−p)σ′))\displaystyle D_{\mathbb{M}}\bigl(p\rho+(1-p)\rho^{\prime}\,|\hskip-1.13809pt|\,p\sigma+(1-p)\sigma^{\prime}\bigr)=D\Bigl(\mathcal{M}\bigl(p\rho+(1-p)\rho^{\prime}\bigr)\Big|\hskip-1.70717pt\Big|\mathcal{M}\bigl(p\sigma+(1-p)\sigma^{\prime}\bigr)\Bigr)
≤p​D​(∑xtr⁡(Mx​ρ)​|x⟩​⟨x|​||∑xtr⁡(Mx​σ)|​x⟩​⟨x|)+(1−p)​D​(∑xtr⁡(Mx​ρ′)​|x⟩​⟨x|​||∑xtr⁡(Mx​σ′)|​x⟩​⟨x|)\displaystyle\leq p\,D\Bigl(\sum_{x}\mathrm{tr}(M_{x}\rho)|x\rangle\!\langle x|\Big|\hskip-1.70717pt\Big|\sum_{x}\mathrm{tr}(M_{x}\sigma)|x\rangle\!\langle x|\Bigr)+(1-p)\,D\Bigl(\sum_{x}\mathrm{tr}(M_{x}\rho^{\prime})|x\rangle\!\langle x|\Big|\hskip-1.70717pt\Big|\sum_{x}\mathrm{tr}(M_{x}\sigma^{\prime})|x\rangle\!\langle x|\Bigr)
≤pD𝕄(ρ||σ)+(1−p)D𝕄(ρ′||σ′).\displaystyle\leq pD_{\mathbb{M}}(\rho|\hskip-1.13809pt|\sigma)+(1-p)D_{\mathbb{M}}(\rho^{\prime}|\hskip-1.13809pt|\sigma^{\prime})\ . (151)

∎

Lemma B.4.

For density operators ρ\rho, σ\sigma, and σ′\sigma^{\prime} and p∈[0,1]p\in[0,1] the measured relative entropy satisfies

D𝕄(ρ||pσ+(1−p)σ′)≤pD𝕄(ρ||σ)+(1−p)D𝕄(ρ||σ′).\displaystyle D_{\mathbb{M}}\bigl(\rho|\hskip-1.13809pt|p\sigma+(1-p)\sigma^{\prime}\bigr)\leq p\,D_{\mathbb{M}}(\rho|\hskip-1.13809pt|\sigma)+(1-p)\,D_{\mathbb{M}}(\rho|\hskip-1.13809pt|\sigma^{\prime})\ . (152)
Proof.

For any measurement ℳ\mathcal{M},

D(ℳ(ρ)||ℳ(pσ+(1−p)σ′))\displaystyle D\bigl(\mathcal{M}(\rho)|\hskip-1.13809pt|\mathcal{M}(p\sigma+(1-p)\sigma^{\prime})\bigr) =D(ℳ(ρ)||pℳ(σ)+(1−p)ℳ(σ′))\displaystyle=D\bigl(\mathcal{M}(\rho)|\hskip-1.13809pt|\,p\,\mathcal{M}(\sigma)+(1-p)\mathcal{M}(\sigma^{\prime})\bigr)
≤pD(ℳ(ρ)||ℳ(σ))+(1−p)D(ℳ(ρ)||ℳ(σ′))\displaystyle\leq p\,D\bigl(\mathcal{M}(\rho)|\hskip-1.13809pt|\mathcal{M}(\sigma)\bigr)+(1-p)\,D\bigl(\mathcal{M}(\rho)|\hskip-1.13809pt|\mathcal{M}(\sigma^{\prime})\bigr)
≤pD𝕄(ρ||σ)+(1−p)D𝕄(ρ||σ′),\displaystyle\leq pD_{\mathbb{M}}(\rho|\hskip-1.13809pt|\sigma)+(1-p)D_{\mathbb{M}}(\rho|\hskip-1.13809pt|\sigma^{\prime})\ , (153)

where the first inequality step uses the convexity of the relative entropy [23, Theorem 11.12]. Taking the supremum over ℳ\mathcal{M}, we get the desired result. ∎

Appendix C Basic topological facts

For completeness we state here some standard topological facts about density operators and trace-preserving completely positive maps.

Lemma C.1.

Let α∈ℝ+\alpha\in\mathbb{R}^{+}. The space of non-negative operators on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space EE with trace smaller or equal to α\alpha (respectively equal to α\alpha) is compact.

Proof.

Let D′​(E):={ρ∈Pos⁡(E):tr⁡(ρ)≤α}\mathrm{D}^{\prime}(E):=\{\rho\in\mathrm{Pos}(E):\mathrm{tr}(\rho)\leq\alpha\} denote the set non-negative operators on EE with trace not larger than one, where Pos⁡(E)\mathrm{Pos}(E) is the set of non-negative operators on EE. Consider the ball ℬ:={e∈E:‖e‖≤α}\mathcal{B}:=\{e\in E:\left\lVert e\right\rVert\leq\alpha\} which is compact. The function ℬ∋e↦f⁡(e)=e​e†∈D′​(E)\mathcal{B}\ni e\mapsto f(e)=ee^{\dagger}\in\mathrm{D}^{\prime}(E) is continuous and thus the set f(ℬ)={ee†:e∈E,‖e‖≤α}f(\mathcal{B})=\{ee^{\dagger}:e\in E,\left\lVert e\right\rVert\leq\alpha\} is compact, as continuous functions map compact sets to compact sets. By the spectral theorem it follows that D′​(E)=conv​f​(ℬ)\mathrm{D}^{\prime}(E)=\mathrm{conv}f(\mathcal{B}). As the convex hull of every compact set is compact this proves the assertion. The same argumentation (by replacing the inequalities with equalities) proves that the set of non-negative operators on EE with trace α\alpha is compact. ∎

Lemma C.2.

Let EE, GG be finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces and let σG∈Pos⁡(G)\sigma_{G}\in\mathrm{Pos}(G). The space of non-negative operators on E⊗GE\otimes G with a marginal on GG smaller or equal to σG\sigma_{G} (respectively equal to σG\sigma_{G}) is compact.

Proof.

Let σG∈Pos⁡(G)\sigma_{G}\in\mathrm{Pos}(G). By Lemma C.1, the set of non-negative operators on E⊗GE\otimes G with trace not larger than α∈ℝ+\alpha\in\mathbb{R}^{+} is compact. The set {X∈E⊗G:trE​(X)≤ρG}\{X\in E\otimes G:\mathrm{tr}_{E}(X)\leq\rho_{G}\} is closed. The intersection of a compact set and a closed set is compact which implies that {X∈Pos⁡(E⊗G):trE​(X)≤ρG}\{X\in\mathrm{Pos}(E\otimes G):\mathrm{tr}_{E}(X)\leq\rho_{G}\} is compact. Since the set {X∈E⊗G:trE​(X)=ρG}\{X\in E\otimes G:\mathrm{tr}_{E}(X)=\rho_{G}\} is closed the same argumentation shows that {X∈Pos⁡(E⊗G):trE​(X)=ρG}\{X\in\mathrm{Pos}(E\otimes G):\mathrm{tr}_{E}(X)=\rho_{G}\} is compact. ∎

Remark C.3.

Let EE and GG be two finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. The space of trace-non-increasing (respectively trace-preserving) completely positive maps from EE to GG is compact. To see this note that Lemma C.2 implies that the set ℱ:={X∈Pos⁡(E⊗G):trG​(X)≤idE}\mathcal{F}:=\{X\in\mathrm{Pos}(E\otimes G):\mathrm{tr}_{G}(X)\leq\mathrm{id}_{E}\} is compact. By the Choi-Jamiolkowski representation ℱ\mathcal{F} is however isomorphic to the set of all trace-non-increasing completely positive maps from EE to GG. The same argumentation applied to the set ℱ:={X∈Pos⁡(E⊗G):trG​(X)=idE}\mathcal{F}:=\{X\in\mathrm{Pos}(E\otimes G):\mathrm{tr}_{G}(X)=\mathrm{id}_{E}\} shows that the set of trace-preserving completely positive maps from EE to GG is compact.

Lemma C.4.

Let GG and KK be finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces and let σE​G​K∈D⁡(E⊗G⊗K)\sigma_{EGK}\in\mathrm{D}(E\otimes G\otimes K). The mapping TPCP⁡(G,G⊗K)∋ℛ↦F⁡(σE​G​K,ℛG→G​K​(σE​G​K))∈[0,1]\mathrm{TPCP}(G,G\otimes K)\ni\mathcal{R}\mapsto F(\sigma_{EGK},\mathcal{R}_{G\to GK}(\sigma_{EGK}))\in[0,1] is continuous.

Proof.

This follows directly from the continuity of ℛ↦ℛG→G​K​(σE​G)\mathcal{R}\mapsto\mathcal{R}_{G\to GK}(\sigma_{EG}) and the continuity of the fidelity (see, e.g., Lemma B.9 of [11]). ∎

Lemma C.5.

Let EE, GG, and KK be separable Hilbert spaces and ℛ∈TPCP⁡(G,K)\mathcal{R}\in\mathrm{TPCP}(G,K). Then the mapping D⁡(E⊗G)∋X↦ℐE⊗ℛG→K​(XE​G)∈D⁡(E⊗K)\mathrm{D}(E\otimes G)\ni\penalty\ X\mapsto\mathcal{I}_{E}\otimes\mathcal{R}_{G\to K}(X_{EG})\in\mathrm{D}(E\otimes K) is continuous.

Proof.

As the map is linear it suffices to show that it is bounded. For that we can decompose X=P−NX=P-N with PP and NN orthogonal non-negative operators. Then we have

‖ℐE⊗ℛG→K​(X)‖1≤‖ℐE⊗ℛG→K​(P)‖1+‖ℐE⊗ℛG→K​(N)‖1=tr⁡(P)+tr⁡(N)=‖X‖1.\displaystyle\|\mathcal{I}_{E}\otimes\mathcal{R}_{G\to K}(X)\|_{1}\leq\|\mathcal{I}_{E}\otimes\mathcal{R}_{G\to K}(P)\|_{1}+\|\mathcal{I}_{E}\otimes\mathcal{R}_{G\to K}(N)\|_{1}=\mathrm{tr}(P)+\mathrm{tr}(N)=\|X\|_{1}\ . (154)

∎

Appendix D Touching sets lemma

We prove here a basic fact that is used in the proof of Theorem 2.1.

Lemma D.1.

Let K0K_{0} and K1K_{1} be two sets such that K0∪K1=[0,1]K_{0}\cup K_{1}=[0,1] and 0∈K00\in K_{0}, 1∈K11\in K_{1}. Then for any δ>0\delta>0 there exists u∈K0u\in K_{0} and v∈K1v\in K_{1} such that 0≤v−u≤δ0\leq v-u\leq\delta.

Proof.

We define μ:=infK1\mu:=\inf K_{1} and distinguish between the two cases μ∈K0\mu\in K_{0} and μ∉K0\mu\not\in K_{0}.

If μ∈K0\mu\in K_{0}, it suffices to show that for any δ>0\delta>0 we have [μ,μ+δ]∩K1≠∅[\mu,\mu+\delta]\cap K_{1}\neq\emptyset, since by choosing u=μu=\mu this implies that u∈K0u\in K_{0} and that there exists a v∈[μ,μ+δ]v\in[\mu,\mu+\delta] such that v∈K1v\in K_{1}. By contradiction, we assume that [μ,μ+δ]∩K1=∅[\mu,\mu+\delta]\cap K_{1}=\emptyset. This implies that either infK1<μ\inf K_{1}<\mu or infK1≥μ+δ\inf K_{1}\geq\mu+\delta, which contradicts μ:=infK1\mu:=\inf K_{1}.

If μ∉K0\mu\not\in K_{0} it suffices to show that for any δ>0\delta>0 we have [μ−δ,μ]∩K0≠∅[\mu-\delta,\mu]\cap K_{0}\neq\emptyset, since by choosing v=μv=\mu this ensures that v∈K1v\in K_{1} and that there exists a u∈[μ−δ,μ]u\in[\mu-\delta,\mu] such that u∈K0u\in K_{0}. Assume by contradiction that [μ−δ,μ]∩K0=∅[\mu-\delta,\mu]\cap K_{0}=\emptyset, which implies that [μ−δ,μ]⊂K1[\mu-\delta,\mu]\subset K_{1}. This however contradicts μ:=infK1\mu:=\inf K_{1}.

∎

Appendix E Properties of projected states

We first prove variant of the gentle measurement lemma [34], which is used repeatedly in the proof of Theorem 2.1.

Lemma E.1.

Let EE and GG be separable Hilbert spaces and let ΠG\Pi_{G} be a finite-rank projector on GG. For any non-negative operator σE​G\sigma_{EG} on E⊗GE\otimes G we have

F​(σE​G,(idE⊗ΠG)​σE​G​(idE⊗ΠG)tr⁡((idE⊗ΠG)​σE​G))2≥tr⁡(ΠG​σE​G)\displaystyle F\!\left(\sigma_{EG},\frac{(\mathrm{id}_{E}\otimes\Pi_{G})\sigma_{EG}(\mathrm{id}_{E}\otimes\Pi_{G})}{\mathrm{tr}\bigl((\mathrm{id}_{E}\otimes\Pi_{G})\sigma_{EG}\bigr)}\right)^{2}\geq\mathrm{tr}(\Pi_{G}\sigma_{EG}) (155)

and

F⁡(σE​G,(idE⊗ΠG)​σE​G​(idE⊗ΠG))≥tr⁡(ΠG​σE​G).\displaystyle F\bigl(\sigma_{EG},(\mathrm{id}_{E}\otimes\Pi_{G})\sigma_{EG}(\mathrm{id}_{E}\otimes\Pi_{G})\bigr)\geq\mathrm{tr}(\Pi_{G}\sigma_{EG})\ . (156)
Proof.

Let |ψ⟩|\psi\rangle be a purification of σE​G\sigma_{EG} then by Uhlmann’s theorem [30] we find

F​(σE​G,(idE⊗ΠG)​σE​G​(idE⊗ΠG)tr⁡((idE⊗ΠG)​σE​G))2≥(⟨ψ|ΠG|ψ⟩)2tr⁡((idE⊗ΠG)​σE​G)=tr⁡(ΠG​σE​G)\displaystyle F\!\left(\sigma_{EG},\frac{(\mathrm{id}_{E}\otimes\Pi_{G})\sigma_{EG}(\mathrm{id}_{E}\otimes\Pi_{G})}{\mathrm{tr}\bigl((\mathrm{id}_{E}\otimes\Pi_{G})\sigma_{EG}\bigr)}\right)^{2}\geq\frac{(\langle\psi|\Pi_{G}|\psi\rangle)^{2}}{\mathrm{tr}\bigl((\mathrm{id}_{E}\otimes\Pi_{G})\sigma_{EG}\bigr)}=\mathrm{tr}(\Pi_{G}\sigma_{EG}) (157)

and

F​(σE​G,(idE⊗ΠG)​σE​G​(idE⊗ΠG))2≥(⟨ψ|ΠG|ψ⟩)2=tr​(ΠG​σE​G)2.\displaystyle F\bigl(\sigma_{EG},(\mathrm{id}_{E}\otimes\Pi_{G})\sigma_{EG}(\mathrm{id}_{E}\otimes\Pi_{G})\bigr)^{2}\geq(\langle\psi|\Pi_{G}|\psi\rangle)^{2}=\mathrm{tr}(\Pi_{G}\sigma_{EG})^{2}\ . (158)

∎

We next prove a basic statement about converging projectors that is used several times in the proof of Theorem 2.1.

Lemma E.2.

Let EE be a separable Hilbert space and let {ΠEe}e∈E\{\Pi_{E}^{e}\}_{e\in E} be a sequence of finite-rank projectors on EE which converges to idE\mathrm{id}_{E} with respect to the weak operator topology. Then for any density operator σE\sigma_{E} on EE we have lime→∞tr⁡(ΠEe​σE)=tr⁡(σE)\lim_{e\to\infty}\mathrm{tr}(\Pi_{E}^{e}\sigma_{E})=\mathrm{tr}(\sigma_{E}).

Proof.

By assumption the Hilbert space EE is separable which implies that any state σE\sigma_{E} can be written as σE=∑ipi​|xi⟩​⟨xi|\sigma_{E}=\sum_{i}p_{i}|x_{i}\rangle\!\langle x_{i}|, where pi≥0p_{i}\geq 0, ∑ipi=1\sum_{i}p_{i}=1 and {|xi⟩}i\{|x_{i}\rangle\}_{i} is an orthonormal basis on EE. As the sequence {ΠEe}e∈ℕ\{\Pi_{E}^{e}\}_{e\in\mathbb{N}} weakly converges to idE\mathrm{id}_{E}, we find

lime→∞tr⁡(ΠEe​σE)=lime→∞∑ipi​⟨xi|ΠEe|xi⟩=∑ipi​lime→∞⟨xi|ΠEe|xi⟩=∑ipi​⟨xi​|idE|​xi⟩=tr⁡(σE),\displaystyle\lim_{e\to\infty}\mathrm{tr}(\Pi_{E}^{e}\sigma_{E})=\lim_{e\to\infty}\sum_{i}p_{i}\langle x_{i}|\Pi_{E}^{e}|x_{i}\rangle=\sum_{i}p_{i}\lim_{e\to\infty}\langle x_{i}|\Pi_{E}^{e}|x_{i}\rangle=\sum_{i}p_{i}\langle x_{i}|\mathrm{id}_{E}|x_{i}\rangle=\mathrm{tr}(\sigma_{E})\ , (159)

where the second step uses the dominated convergence theorem that is applicable since |⟨xi|ΠEe|xi⟩|≤|⟨xi|idE|xi⟩||\langle x_{i}|\Pi_{E}^{e}|x_{i}\rangle|\leq|\langle x_{i}|\mathrm{id}_{E}|x_{i}\rangle| for all e∈ℕe\in\mathbb{N}. ∎

Let EE and GG be separable Hilbert spaces and let 𝒮\mathcal{S} denote the set of bipartite density operators on E⊗GE\otimes G with a fixed marginal σG\sigma_{G} on GG. Let {ΠEe}e∈ℕ\{\Pi_{E}^{e}\}_{e\in\mathbb{N}} be a sequence of projectors with rank ee that weakly converge to idE\mathrm{id}_{E} and 𝒮e\mathcal{S}^{e} be the set of bipartite states on E⊗GE\otimes G whose marginal on EE is contained in the support of ΠEe\Pi^{e}_{E} and whose marginal on GG is identical to σG\sigma_{G}.

Lemma E.3.

For every σE​G∈𝒮\sigma_{EG}\in\mathcal{S} there exists a sequence {σE​Ge}e∈ℕ\{\sigma_{EG}^{e}\}_{e\in\mathbb{N}} with σE​Ge∈𝒮e\sigma_{EG}^{e}\in\mathcal{S}^{e} that converges to σE​G\sigma_{EG} with respect to the trace norm.

Proof.

For σE​G∈𝒮\sigma_{EG}\in\mathcal{S}, let

σ¯E​Ge:=(ΠEe⊗idG)​σE​G​(ΠEe⊗idG)tr⁡((ΠEe⊗idG)​σE​G),\displaystyle\bar{\sigma}_{EG}^{e}:=\frac{(\Pi_{E}^{e}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{G})\sigma_{EG}(\Pi_{E}^{e}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{G})}{\mathrm{tr}\bigl((\Pi_{E}^{e}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{G})\sigma_{EG}\bigr)}\ , (160)

which has the desired support on EE, however, σ¯Ge≠σG\bar{\sigma}_{G}^{e}\neq\sigma_{G} in general. This is fixed by considering

σE​Ge:=tr⁡((ΠEe⊗idG)​σE​G)​σ¯E​Ge+|0⟩​⟨0|E⊗trE​((ΠEe⟂⊗idG)​σE​G​(ΠEe⟂⊗idG))G,\displaystyle\sigma_{EG}^{e}:=\mathrm{tr}\bigl((\Pi_{E}^{e}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{G})\sigma_{EG}\bigr)\bar{\sigma}_{EG}^{e}+|0\rangle\!\langle 0|_{E}\otimes\mathrm{tr}_{E}\bigl((\Pi_{E}^{e\perp}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{G})\sigma_{EG}(\Pi_{E}^{e\perp}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{G})\bigr)_{G}\ , (161)

where |0⟩E|0\rangle_{E} is a normalized state on EE. Since the partial trace on EE is cyclic on EE we obtain

σGe=trE​(σE​Ge)=trE​((ΠEe⊗idG)​σE​G​(ΠEe⊗idG))+trE​((ΠEe⟂⊗idG)​σE​G​(ΠEe⟂⊗idG))=trE​((ΠEe⊗idG)​σE​G)+trE​((ΠEe⟂⊗idG)​σE​G)=trE​(σE​G)=σG.\sigma_{G}^{e}=\mathrm{tr}_{E}(\sigma_{EG}^{e})=\mathrm{tr}_{E}\bigl((\Pi_{E}^{e}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{G})\sigma_{EG}(\Pi_{E}^{e}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{G})\bigr)+\mathrm{tr}_{E}\bigl((\Pi_{E}^{e\perp}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{G})\sigma_{EG}(\Pi_{E}^{e\perp}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{G})\bigr)\\ =\mathrm{tr}_{E}\bigl((\Pi_{E}^{e}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{G})\sigma_{EG}\bigr)+\mathrm{tr}_{E}\bigl((\Pi_{E}^{e\perp}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{G})\sigma_{EG}\bigr)=\mathrm{tr}_{E}(\sigma_{EG})=\sigma_{G}\ . (162)

By the multiplicativity of the trace norm under tensor products and since ‖A‖1=tr⁡(A†​A)\left\lVert A\right\rVert_{1}=\mathrm{tr}(\sqrt{A^{\dagger}A}), the triangle inequality implies that

‖σ¯E​Ge−σE​Ge‖1≤1−tr⁡((ΠEe⊗idG)​σE​G)+‖trE​((ΠEe⟂⊗idG)​σE​G​(ΠEe⟂⊗idG))‖1=1−tr⁡((ΠEe⊗idG)​σE​G)+tr⁡((ΠEe⟂⊗idG)​σE​G)=2​(1−tr⁡(ΠEe​σE)).\left\lVert\bar{\sigma}_{EG}^{e}-\sigma_{EG}^{e}\right\rVert_{1}\leq 1-\mathrm{tr}\bigl((\Pi_{E}^{e}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{G})\sigma_{EG}\bigr)+\left\lVert\mathrm{tr}_{E}\bigl((\Pi_{E}^{e\perp}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{G})\sigma_{EG}(\Pi_{E}^{e\perp}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{G})\bigr)\right\rVert_{1}\\ =1-\mathrm{tr}\bigl((\Pi_{E}^{e}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{G})\sigma_{EG}\bigr)+\mathrm{tr}\bigl((\Pi_{E}^{e\perp}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{G})\sigma_{EG}\bigr)=2\bigl(1-\mathrm{tr}(\Pi_{E}^{e}\sigma_{E})\bigr)\ . (163)

Lemma E.2 now implies that lime→∞tr⁡(ΠEe​σE)=1\lim_{e\to\infty}\mathrm{tr}(\Pi_{E}^{e}\sigma_{E})=1. We note that the sequence {σ¯E​Ge}e∈ℕ\{\bar{\sigma}_{EG}^{e}\}_{e\in\mathbb{N}} converges to σE​G\sigma_{EG} in the trace norm since by the Fuchs-van de Graaf inequality [12], Lemma E.1 and Lemma E.2

lime→∞‖σE​G−σ¯E​Ge‖1≤lime→∞2​1−F​(σE​G,σ¯E​Ge)2≤lime→∞2​1−tr⁡(ΠEe​σE)=0.\displaystyle\lim_{e\to\infty}\left\lVert\sigma_{EG}-\bar{\sigma}_{EG}^{e}\right\rVert_{1}\leq\lim_{e\to\infty}2\sqrt{1-F(\sigma_{EG},\bar{\sigma}_{EG}^{e})^{2}}\leq\lim_{e\to\infty}2\sqrt{1-\mathrm{tr}(\Pi_{E}^{e}\sigma_{E})}=0\ . (164)

Combining this with (163) and the triangle inequality proves that {σE​Ge}e∈ℕ\{\sigma_{EG}^{e}\}_{e\in\mathbb{N}} converges to σE​G\sigma_{EG} in the trace norm. ∎

Appendix F The transpose map is not square-root optimal

As discussed in Section 6, for pure states ρA​B​C\rho_{ABC} it is known [2] that

F​(A;C|B)ρ≤F⁡(ρA​B​C,𝒯B→B​C​(ρA​B))\displaystyle F(A;C|B)_{\rho}\leq\sqrt{F\big(\rho_{ABC},\mathcal{T}_{B\to BC}(\rho_{AB})\big)}\ (165)

holds for 𝒯B→B​C\mathcal{T}_{B\to BC} the transpose map. In this appendix we show that (165) does not hold for all mixed states. Let dimA=dimB=dimC=2\dim A=\dim B=\dim C=2 and consider the state

ρA​B​C=12​|0⟩​⟨0|A⊗|0⟩​⟨0|B⊗|0⟩​⟨0|C+18|1⟩​⟨1|A⊗idB​C.\displaystyle\rho_{ABC}=\frac{1}{2}|0\rangle\!\langle 0|_{A}\otimes|0\rangle\!\langle 0|_{B}\otimes|0\rangle\!\langle 0|_{C}+\frac{1}{8}|1\rangle\!\langle 1|_{A}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{BC}\ . (166)

The transpose map satisfies

𝒯B→B​C​(|0⟩​⟨0|B)=56​|00⟩​⟨00|B​C+16|01⟩​⟨01|B​Cand𝒯B→B​C​(|1⟩​⟨1|B)=12​|10⟩​⟨10|B​C+12|11⟩​⟨11|B​C.\displaystyle\mathcal{T}_{B\to BC}(|0\rangle\!\langle 0|_{B})=\frac{5}{6}|00\rangle\!\langle 00|_{BC}+\frac{1}{6}|01\rangle\!\langle 01|_{BC}\quad\text{and}\quad\mathcal{T}_{B\to BC}(|1\rangle\!\langle 1|_{B})=\frac{1}{2}|10\rangle\!\langle 10|_{BC}+\frac{1}{2}|11\rangle\!\langle 11|_{BC}\ . (167)

If we consider a recovery map ℛB→B​C\mathcal{R}_{B\to BC} that is defined by

ℛB→B​C​(|0⟩​⟨0|B)=|00⟩​⟨00|B​C and ℛB→B​C​(|1⟩​⟨1|B)=13​(|01⟩​⟨01|B​C+|10⟩​⟨10|B​C+|11⟩​⟨11|B​C),\displaystyle\mathcal{R}_{B\to BC}(|0\rangle\!\langle 0|_{B})=|00\rangle\!\langle 00|_{BC}\quad\text{ and }\quad\mathcal{R}_{B\to BC}(|1\rangle\!\langle 1|_{B})=\frac{1}{3}\left(|01\rangle\!\langle 01|_{BC}+|10\rangle\!\langle 10|_{BC}+|11\rangle\!\langle 11|_{BC}\right)\ , (168)

we find F⁡(ρA​B​C,ℛB→B​C​(ρA​B))>0.9829F(\rho_{ABC},\mathcal{R}_{B\to BC}(\rho_{AB}))>0.9829 and F⁡(ρA​B​C,𝒯B→B​C​(ρA​B))<0.9696\sqrt{F(\rho_{ABC},\mathcal{T}_{B\to BC}(\rho_{AB}))}<0.9696, which shows that (165) cannot hold since F⁡(ρA​B​C,ℛB→B​C​(ρA​B))≤F​(A;C|B)ρF\bigl(\rho_{ABC},\mathcal{R}_{B\to BC}(\rho_{AB})\bigr)\leq F(A;C|B)_{\rho}.

This does not show that one cannot prove a non-trivial guarantee on the performance of the transpose map relative to the optimal recovery map, but it suggests that such a guarantee would have to be worse than the square root (and actually worse that the fourth root as well using another example), or perhaps it is more naturally expressed using a different distance measure (using similar examples, the trace distance does not seem to be a good candidate, either). We further note that this example does not show that (2) is wrong for the transpose map.
